chinese.name: Chinese-style Order
baseOrder: Steamed or stir-fried protein (chicken, tofu, shrimp-free seafood, or beef) over deep-fried
Brown rice if it's offered, or a smaller portion of white rice
A vegetable side (broccoli, bok choy, snap peas) in addition to the main
Sauce on the side — a little goes further than it looks
Skip the fried appetizer if the main dish is already fried
whyItWorks: Steamed and stir-fried dishes keep saturated fat much lower than deep-fried ones
Ordering a vegetable side is the single easiest fiber upgrade at most Chinese restaurants
Rice control is the biggest lever for keeping this meal from feeling heavy afterward
modifications: Ask for less oil or "light sauce" if the kitchen allows it
Order one fewer fried item and one more vegetable side
Split a large entree instead of finishing the whole portion in one sitting
watchOuts: Sauces are a major sodium and sugar source — sweet and sour, general tso's, and orange sauce especially
Fried rice and lo mein add up fast on refined carbs
If you have a shellfish allergy, double-check shared woks and fryer oil with the kitchen
chinese.dentalTip: Sticky sweet sauces are the main dental risk here — rinse with water after, especially if dessert-sweet sauces were involved.
chinese.cholesterolTip: Steamed or stir-fried with sauce on the side keeps this genuinely reasonable for your LDL/ApoB goals. Fried plus heavy sauce is where it stops being that.

sandwich.name: Sandwich
baseOrder: Whole grain or whole wheat bread over white
A real protein layer — turkey, chicken, egg, or hummus
Vegetables piled in — lettuce, tomato, cucumber, peppers
A thin spread rather than a thick layer of mayo or cheese
A side salad or fruit instead of chips, most of the time
whyItWorks: Whole grain bread adds fiber that white bread skips entirely
A real protein layer keeps you full instead of snacky an hour later
Piling on vegetables is free volume and free fiber
modifications: Ask for mayo or cheese on the side, or go half portion
Add an extra vegetable instead of an extra cheese slice
Choose a side salad or fruit cup over chips when it's an option
watchOuts: Double meat plus double cheese plus mayo adds up in saturated fat fast
Deli meats can be high in sodium — balance with lower-sodium sides
Chips and a sugary drink can quietly double the meal's impact
sandwich.dentalTip: Bread is fairly gentle on teeth. If there's a sweet drink alongside, rinse with water after.
sandwich.cholesterolTip: The protein and spread choices matter most — lean protein and a light spread keep this solidly cholesterol-friendly.

noodles.name: Noodle Dish
baseOrder: Broth-based or lightly-sauced noodles over cream-based or deep-fried
A real protein — chicken, tofu, egg, or lean beef
Vegetables mixed in, not just on the side
A smaller noodle portion with extra broth or vegetables to fill the bowl
Sauce or chili oil added a little at a time, not all at once
whyItWorks: Broth-based noodle dishes are naturally lighter than cream or deep-fried versions
Mixing vegetables directly in adds fiber without needing a separate side
A smaller noodle portion still feels like a full bowl once vegetables fill it out
modifications: Ask for a vegetable-forward version, or extra vegetables mixed in
Choose broth or light sauce over cream sauce when it's an option
Add protein if the dish is mostly noodles with little else
watchOuts: Cream sauces (alfredo-style, carbonara-style) are a major saturated fat source
Noodle dishes are easy to underestimate the sodium in — sauces and broths add up
A noodle-only bowl with little protein won't keep you full very long
noodles.dentalTip: Not much dental risk from the noodles themselves — watch for very acidic or spicy chili sauces if your teeth feel sensitive that day.
noodles.cholesterolTip: Broth or light-sauce versions with real protein and vegetables are a solid choice. Cream sauce is the one thing worth trading up from most days.

other.name: Your Meal
baseOrder: A real protein source — fish, tofu, beans, chicken, or eggs
At least one serving of vegetables or fruit
A whole grain or fiber-rich carb over a refined one, when there's a choice
A sauce or dressing on the side so you're in control of it
Water alongside the meal, especially if anything is salty or sweet
whyItWorks: Protein plus fiber is the combination that keeps you full and your energy steady
Vegetables are one of the most reliable levers for both fiber and general wellness
Sauce on the side means the flavor is still there, just on your terms
modifications: Add a vegetable or fruit if the meal doesn't already have one
Add a protein source if the meal is mostly carbs
Ask for sauce or dressing on the side
watchOuts: Without seeing the specific dish, sodium and added sugar are the two things most worth a second look
If anything is fried, it's usually the biggest single lever on saturated fat
Double-check any shellfish-adjacent ingredients given your allergy
other.dentalTip: Drink water after the meal, and go easy on lingering over anything sweet or acidic.
other.cholesterolTip: Lean toward fish, tofu, and beans over red meat and creamy sauces when you have the choice — small, repeatable swaps add up.
